papers.title_in_file: Comparing Classical and Quantum Machine Learning for Regression in High Energy Physics Collision Data
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, experimental setup, results and discussion (section IV), conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing four classical regressors with four quantum counterparts on simulated LHC collision data.

assertions.value: The authors report that the classical models, in particular the CNN and LSTM, reach marginally better quantitative performance than their quantum counterparts under current hardware and dataset constraints, while the quantum models reach competitive accuracy with substantially fewer trainable parameters.
quotes: Classical architectures, and in particular the CNN and LSTM, achieve marginally better quantitative performance under current hardware and dataset constraints.
Quantum models, however, reach competitive accuracy with substantially fewer trainable parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QCNN reproduces the performance of the deep classical CNN using only four qubits and a circuit of depth three.
quotes: the QCNN reproduces the performance of the deep classical CNN using only four qubits and a circuit of depth three
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study.
assertions.reader_inference: The results table lists the QCNN as 2 convolution layers plus 1 fully connected layer, so the abstract's depth phrase may count layers differently.

assertions.value: The authors state that all models are trained on simulated proton-proton collision events with electron-positron and muon-antimuon final states from the CERN Open Data portal.
quotes: All models are trained on simulated proton-proton collision events with electron-positron and muon-antimuon final states from the CERN Open Data portal
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its data setup, Abstract p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that a full resource analysis accounting for shot budget alongside parameter count would be necessary before drawing strong hardware-efficiency conclusions.
quotes: A full resource analysis that accounts for shot budget alongside parameter count would be necessary before drawing strong hardware-efficiency conclusions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own caveat, Section IV.C p.7.

quotes: We demonstrate that our strategy allows us to implement a Toffoli gate with sufficiently high fidelity, as compared to the other similar techniques.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the ansatz is a sequence of parametrized unitaries describing at most two-qubit nearest neighbour interactions, and that the approach is applied in simulation, with and without stochastic noise.

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proposing a graph-connectivity quantum algorithm built from non-unitary ZX-calculus gates, with a numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a quantum algorithm for determining graph connectedness using a constant number of measurements, and state that it needs only two measurements to compute the result with a certainty of p = 3/4.
